items.title: Frank Goudie Interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, these guys like, these guys like Milky... [INTERVIEWEE] Yes. That's, that has, that has helped me a lot. Yeah. Him and, and, and Patton.

ctx.x: When I came back, I had to do a lot of things. And I never did want to listen too much at record to copy anybody first, because I realized I can't do what they do, as I mentioned before. Yeah. So what I had to do was close my eyes and picture all those famous guys, especially as I've worked with Frank Matthew for a long time. And I knew how he played, and I still couldn't picture, you know, dogs when I heard him and hear different clarinet players from New Orleans that even wasn't known. And I had to picture all…

Well, these guys like, these guys like Milky, I think, escaped Frank what so many old fake cats have done. Milky seems to play a more, shall we say, more real, earthy trombones, the real thing, because he isn't imitating. You understand? Yes. He's playing the New Orleans idiom, but he's not imitating.
Yes. That's, that has, that has helped me a lot. Yeah. Him and, and, and Patton.
